findings.title: Separate count and insert steps let concurrent new devices exceed the limit.
findings.body:
`CountDevices` and the following INSERT/upsert do not run in the same transaction or under a lock. When the count is at `limit-1`, several new devices authenticating at the same moment all see `count < limit` and all get inserted, so the configured limit is exceeded.

Fix: do the check and the insert atomically, either with a conditional insert (`INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < ?`) or inside one transaction that holds a suitable lock.

findings.title: The callback rewrites the captured `args` slice, so a retried session sends a corrupted argument list.
findings.body:
`args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` reassigns the outer `args` variable inside the `WithDbSession` callback. If the session runs the callback again (for example, when it retries after SQLite reports 'database is locked'), the query string is prepended a second time. `Exec` then gets the wrong number and order of parameters, and the update fails or misbinds.

Fix: build the argument list once, outside the closure, or use a local variable inside it:

```go
execArgs := append([]interface{}{query}, args...)
```

findings.title: The store's constructor now needs a raw `int64` limit, which the wire dependency setup cannot supply if it still uses `ProvideAnonDBStore`.
findings.body:
`ProvideAnonDBStore` now takes `(db.DB, int64)`. `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` builds the store itself and no longer receives `anonstore.AnonStore`. If `pkg/server/wire.go` still lists `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` or binds `AnonStore` (I could not check this from these hunks), wire generation fails because nothing provides an `int64`. Any other consumer that is injected `AnonStore` would also get a different instance, one with no limit applied.

Fix: remove those providers and bindings from wire, or pass `*setting.Cfg` into `ProvideAnonDBStore`.
